sentences.text: JUDGMENT

This judgment arise out of claim petition filed by the claimant against respondents under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred as "Act") praying to award compensation in respect of the injuries sustained by him in the road traffic accident occurred on 26.02.2024.
2.

The case of the claimant in nutshell is that:
On 26.02.2024 at about 7.30am, the petitioner was pedestrian, while the petitioner was proceeding by walk on Tumakuru Road, in front of Hallimane, Yeshwanthapura at Bangalore City, by observing the traffic rules and regulations and also observing the vehicle moments and almost crossed the above said road, at that time the rider of the Motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-05-EG-1249 came from Gowrdhan Theater with a high speed, in a rash and negligent manner, endangering human life and dashed to the petitioner.
Due to impact, the petitioner sustained grievous injuries.

3. It is the further case of the petitioner that, Immediately after the accident, the petitioner was shifted to the nearest Hospital, i.e., K.C.General Hospital, Bangalore and treated as an inpatient from 26.02.2024, underwent surgery and discharged on 13.03.2024 with an advice to take follow up treatment.

So far he has spent more than Rs.1,00,000/- towards hospitalization, conveyance,
medical treatment, attendant and other incidental expenses.

Due to the said accidental injuries,
petitioner is suffering with permanent disability.
He is not able to lead a normal life as prior to the accident.
4. It is the further case of the petitioner that, prior to the accident, the petitioner was hale and healthy, he was a Driver and earning Rs.25,000/- per month.
Due to the accidental injuries, he became permanently disabled and unable to do his profession and not getting his income.

5. The accident has taken place solely due to the rash and negligent riding by the rider of the Motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-05-EG-1249 and in this regard a case has been registered by Yeshwanthapura Traffic Police under Cr.No.19/2024 against the rider of the Motorcycle P/U/Secs.279, 337 of IPC.
Hence, the respondents being the RC owner and the Insurer of the Motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-05-EG-1249 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.

Hence, petitioner prays for award for the total compensation of Rs.20,00,000/-
6.
In response to the notice, the respondents appeared through their respective counsels and filed separate written statements.

6A. The 1st respondent in its written statement has denied the entire petition averments except admitting the ownership of motorcycle bearing No.KA-05-EG-1249 and the same was insured with Vinayakumar B R vs Vinay Raju V on 1 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/168743623/

The respondent further stated that the rider of the vehicle had a valid DL to ride his vehicle.
Further stated that the petitioner himself has contributed to the accident.
He has denied the manner of accident.
Further, he has denied the age, occupation, medical expenses etc., of the petitioner.
Further contended that the compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly excessive and exorbitant.
Therefore, prayed for dismissal of the petition against him.

6B. The 2nd respondent in its written statement has denied the entire petition averments except admitting the issuance of policy in respect of the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-05-EG-1249 in favour of the 1st respondent.
The accident occurred due to the negligence of the petitioner himself.

Without noticing on coming vehicles and was crossing the road in a place not meant for pedestrian crossing and caused the accident as such, the accident caused due to the negligence of the petitioner himself.
Further, it has denied the age, occupation, medical expenses etc., of the petitioner.
Further contended that the compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly excessive and exorbitant.
Therefore, prayed for dismissal of the petition against it.
7. Basing on the pleadings of the parties, the following issues are framed for determination.

Issue No.1: Whether the petitioner proves that, the accident occurred on 26-02-2024 at 07.30am,
due to rash and negligent riding of rider of motorcycle bearing registration Number:
KA-05-EG-1249 and in the said accident petitioner sustained injuries?
Issue No.2: Whether the petitioner is entitled for Compensation?
If so, what is the quantum?
From whom?
Issue No.3: What Order or Award?
8. In order to substantiate the claim petition contention, the petitioner has examined himself as PW.1 and got marked 13 documents as per Exs.P.1 to 13.
Dr.Nagaraj B.N. - Orthopedic Surgeon at Sai Ortho and Dental center and resident of Bangalore got examined as PW.2 and got marked Exs.P.14 & P.15.
He has also got examined Mr.Simon G.A. - MRD at KC General Hospital, Bangalore as PW.3 and got marked Exs.P.16 to P.19.
On the other side, the respondents did not examine any witness nor produced any documents on their behalf.
9. I have heard the arguments canvassed by the learned counsel for the parties.

10. On perusal of oral and documentary evidence led by the parties before this tribunal, my answers to the above issues are as follows:
Issue No.1: Partly in the affirmative, Issue No.2: Partly in affirmative.

In order to substantiate the claim petition contention, the petitioner has examined himself as PW.1.
The petitioner has got examined Dr.Nagaraj B.N. as PW.2 and also got examined one more witness as PW.3.

The details of the exhibits are given in the annexure of the judgment.
12. The chief examination of the PW.1 is nothing but a repetition of plaint averments.
PW.1 has been subjected to the cross examination.
During the cross examination of PW.1, he has deposed that he was alone walking on the service road and going from Hallimane Hotel towards Yashwanthpura.
Further stated that the he observed the motorcycle and it hits to him.
The vehicle number si KA-05-EG- 1249.
The complaint was lodged by himself at hospital when the police came to the hospital as on the date of accident itself.
Before the accident he was working as a Driver.
Now he is not working.
He had a DL.
He has further denied the suggestions of the counsel for the other side.
13. The petitioner has totally relied on the police documents to establish the negligence on the part of the offending vehicle's rider.

The spot mahazar appended to sketch indicates that the petitioner was about crossing the service road from Hallimane Hotel, at that time the motorcycle came from Govardhan Theater with high speed, in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the pedestrian/Petitioner and caused the accident.
The Sketch is also shows the spot of the accident wherein the petitioner was about the cross the road on the left side of the Service road of that too from Hallimane Hotel.
It is undisputed fact that the petitioner was a Driver.
It is worth note herein that the motor vehicle inspection report clinches that no fresh visible damages noticed at the time of inspection.
The accident area is almost crowded area.

The alleged accident was occurred at about 7.30AM, when the said area was almost filled with public as it was alighting time of public from different mode of transport that too from train and bus and also number of public are moving towards their work as the accident date fallen on MONDAY.
As such, it is appears to Court that the accident was not occurred sole negligence on the part of the rider of the offending vehicle.
The petitioner has also not observed the oncoming vehicles.
The rider of the offending vehicle had taken minimal care and caution, the accident might have postponed.

It is no doubt the police have submitted the charge sheet against the rider of the offending vehicle for the offense punishable under section 279, 338 of IPC and Sec.56, 193 of MV Act for not having FC to the vehicle.
It is worth note herein that the final report is not sole basis to come to definite conclusion regarding the rashness as alleged.
The final report is certainly helping toll to the tribunal to ascertain the rashness.
However, the person who alleges about the negligence on the offending vehicle ought to have prove his case by touchstone of preponderance of all probability.
14. The insurance company has taken a contention that the rider of the offending vehicle did not possess a valid driving license.
A perusal of the charge sheet, the police have submitted the charge sheet against the accused or rider of the offending Motorcycle.

The police have referred section 279,
338 of the IPC.
The Court cannot adopt strict liability as conducted in a criminal case to prove rash and negligence on the part of the driver of the respondent vehicle.
But there should be prima-facie materials regarding rash and negligence to fix the owner and insurance company for payment of compensation.
Therefore, a straight jacket formula cannot be adopted in accepting the rash and negligence on the part of the rider of the insured.

Thus in overall consideration, that the accident Vinayakumar B R vs Vinay Raju V on 1 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/168743623/
4 was not occurred sole negligence of offending vehicle's rider.

15. Issue No.2:
The petitioner has produced the wound certificate and call the medical records from the concerned hospital.
The wound certificate (Ex.P8) discloses that, the petitioner has sustained injury to the left leg which is grievous in nature.
In this regard, the petitioner has examined Simon G.A. as PW.3 and got marked Exs.P16 to 19, authorization letter, case sheet, MLC Extract and X- ray.
PW.3 has been subjected to cross examination.
During the cross examination of PW.3 nothing worthwhile is elicited.
Apart from this, petitioner has also got examined Dr.Nagaraj B.N. as PW.2 and got marked Exs.P.14 & 15.
PW.3 has reiterated the petition averments in his chief examination.
The PW.2 has stated in the chief examination affidavit that "on examination, PW.2 diagnosed that the petitioner has sustained left leg both bones fracture.
Petitioner was treated at KC General Hospital with CRIF with IMIL Nail on 08.02.2024 and later discharged on 13.03.2024.
The fractures got united.
The petitioner complains of pain in the left leg, unable to lift weights, unable to sit down, squat and sit cross leg and carry his job as Driver.
On examination it is found that the petitioner has restricted left knee and ankle movements, wasting of the left thigh muscles.
X-ray of the left leg shows fractures are united with impalnt in situ.
The PW.2 has opined that the petitioner has got permanent physical disability of the left lower limb at 42% and to the whole body at 14%.
PW.2 has been cross examined by the counsel for R-2.
During the cross examination of PW.2, he has stated that, presently there is no necessary of treatment to the petitioner.
16. Before discussing on this point, it is necessary to advert to the observations made by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Raj Kumar vs. Ajay Kumar.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court has held that, the provision of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 makes it clear that the award must be just, which means that compensation should, to the extent possible, fully and adequately restore the claimant to the position prior to the accident.
The object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner.

The Court or Tribunal shall have to assess the damages objectively and exclude from consideration any speculation or fancy, though some conjecture with reference to the nature of disability and its consequences, is inevitable.
A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury.

This means that he is to be compensated for his inability to lead a full life, his inability to enjoy those normal amenities which he would have enjoyed but for the injuries, and his inability to earn as much as he used to earn or could have earned.

17. Our Hon'ble High Court has held in a case MFA.811 OF 2015 (MV-I) decided on 18 July, 2019 in between Rajanna @ Raju and another V/s Srinivas and another that "It is necessary to understand the meaning of the expression "permanent disability", which has been elucidated in Rajkumar.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: According to the Hon'ble Supreme Court, disability refers to any restriction or lack of ability to perform an activity in the manner considered normal for a human being.

Permanent disability refers to the residuary incapacity or loss of use of some part of the body, found existing at the end of the period of treatment and recuperation, after achieving the maximum bodily improvement or recovery which is likely to remain for the remainder life of the injured.

Temporary disability refers to the Vinayakumar B R vs Vinay Raju V on 1 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/168743623/
5 incapacity or loss of use of some part of the body on account of the injury, which will cease to exist at the end of the period of treatment and recuperation.

sentences.text: Permanent disability can be either partial or total.

Partial permanent disability refers to a person's inability to perform all the duties and bodily functions that he could perform before the accident, though he is able to perform some of them and is still able to engage in some gainful activity.
Total permanent disability refers to a person's inability to perform any avocation or employment related activities as a result of the accident.

The permanent disabilities that may arise from motor accidents injuries, are of a much wider range when compared to the physical disabilities which are enumerated in the Persons with Disabilities (Equal Opportunities, Protection of Rights and Full Participation) Act, 1995 ("the Disabilities Act",
for short).

entities.text: Persons with Disabilities (Equal Opportunities, Protection of Rights and Full Participation) Act, 1995
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: But if any of the disabilities enumerated in Section 2(i) of the Disabilities Act are the result of injuries sustained in a motor accident, they can be permanent disabilities for the purpose of claiming compensation.

12. Therefore, the Tribunal has to first decide whether there is any permanent disability and, if so,
the extent of such permanent disability.

By considering the dictums of Hon'ble Supreme Court and Our Hon'ble High Court and also evidence led by the medical officer, It is appears to Court that, the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries.
The petition discloses that the petitioner was doing Driving work.
The evidence of the medical officer clearly clinches that on clinical examination, the medical officer has pointed out the difficulties of the injured person to do routine work.
It means, the petitioner is not in position to do the earlier work effectively.
The Hon'ble Supreme Court of India has held in a judgment/decision of 1 ALIVELI MALLAREDDY Vs SURTHANI LINGANNA @ CHINNA LINGANNA & Others.

By considering the age, nature of injuries and treatment, it is appears to Court that the petitioner has suffered disability of the left lower limb at 8.4% (42%  1/5 of limb) to the whole body.

As such,
the petitioner has suffered permanent physical disability of 8.4% to the whole body.
Therefore, the claimant is entitled for the compensation under the following heads.

19. The claimant has contended that he has taken treatment at K.C.General Hospital, Bangalore wherein he took treatment as an inpatient, underwent surgery and discharged with an advise for follow up treatment.
Further, in this regard petitioner has not produced Discharge Summary to show the details of surgery and duration of the treatment.
The petitioner has produced the Medical bills of KC General Hospital and other medical shop bills for a sum of Rs.13,386/- as per Ex.P.11.
There is no contrary evidence to these bills from the respondents.
There is no repeated bills.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for the said amount under the head of Medical Expenses.
As supra said, the petitioner has admitted at KC General Hospital as an inpatient, but he has not produced the Discharge summary of the said hospital.

In the absence of Discharge summary, this court will considered as mentioned in the chief examination of the petitioner that he had taken treatment at KC General Hospital from 26.02.2024 to 13.03.2024 for a period of Fifteen days.
Hence, it is just and proper to award a sum of Rs.500/-per day for attendant and Rs.500/- for food and nourishment charges, which would comes Rs.16,000/-.
A sum of Rs.16,000/- is awarded under the head of attendant, food and nourishment charges.
(ii) LOSS OF EARNING 20.
The claimant has contended that, he was a Driver by profession and earning a sum of Rs.25,000/- per month.
In this regard, the petitioner has not produced any other documents like payslips, Vouchers, Bank Statement etc.,
He has failed to prove his exact income.
So, considering the nature of work notional income of Rs.16,500/-pm. is calculated to award loss of earning, it would meets the ends of justice.
Therefore, I award Rs.8,800/- to the claimant under the head of loss of earning during the treatment.

(b) LOSS OF FUTURE EARNING ON ACCOUNT OF PERMANENT DISABILITY:
21.
The claimant has examined the Doctor to substantiate the disability as PW-2.
As already discussed above, the petitioner was suffered disability.
The medical officer has given physical disability of 14% Points for functional loss of malocclusion.
By considering the nature of injuries and treatment, it is appears to Court that the petitioner has suffered permanent physical disability of 8.4%.
As per the petition averments, the age of the claimant is 24 years.
The Aadhar Card of the petitioner marked at Exs.P10 clearly discloses that, the age of the petitioner was 24 years.
However the medical documents are clearly demonstrates that the age of the petitioner was 24 years at the time of accident.
Therefore, the age of the claimant is considered as 24 years to assess the loss of future earning and the multiplier is 18.
As I have already stated the notional income of the claimant is Rs.16,500/-pm,

The loss of future earning is calculated as Rs.16,500/- (Monthly income) X 12 (Months) X 18 (multiplier) X 8.4%(disability)  100 =Rs.2,99,376/- which is the just and proper compensation payable to claimant.

22. The claimant has undergone pain and suffering during the accident and during the rehabilitation period.
Therefore, I award Rs.1,00,000/- as compensation to the claimant under the head of pain and suffering.
23. As per the version of PW.2, the Petitioner needs another surgery for removal of implants and the estimating cost of the surgery is around Rs.60,000/-.
In this regard neither the petitioner nor PW.2 has produced any estimation bill about further surgery.

As per the evidence of Pws.1 & 2 and looking at the earlier treatment cost and the evidence on record, it appears it would be justifiable if an amount of Rs.20,000/- is awarded to the Petitioner under the head of Future Medical Expenses.

24. The claimant in all entitled for just compensation under the following heads:
Sl. NATURE OF THE HEADS COMPENSATION No. 01 Medical Expenses Rs.13,386=00 02 Loss of income during Rs.8,800 =00 treatment 03 Attendant, Food & Rs.16,000=00 Nourishment charges 04 Pain and Suffering Rs.1,00,000=00 05 Loss of future earning on Rs.2,99,376=00 account of disability 06
Future Medical Expenses Rs.20,000=00 TOTAL Rs.4,57,562=00 25.
The next question is the liability to pay the said compensation.
As I discussed in supra, the petitioner has contributed 10% towards the accident and rider of the offending vehicle has contributed 90% to the accident.
The petitioner proved that as on the date of accident the policy was in force.
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.4,11,805=00(Rs.457562  90100).
Therefore, Respondent No.2 has to indemnify the respondent No.1 and liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, I answer issue No.2 partly in affirmative 26.
Issue No.3:-

In view of my findings to the above Issues, I proceed to pass the following:
-: ORDER :-

The claim petition filed by claimant under section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act,
1988 is allowed in part.

The Petitioner is entitled for  compensation of Rs.4,11,805=00 (Rupees Four Lakhs Eleven Thousands Eight Hundred and Five Only) with interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till realization.
The Respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation to the claimant and directed to deposit the same within 60 days from the date of this judgment.

On deposit of compensation, the claimant is entitled to withdraw entire amount as it was meager amount on proper identification.

Thus in overall consideration, that the accident Vinayakumar B R vs Vinay Raju V on 1 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/168743623/
4 was not occurred sole negligence of offending vehicle's rider.
The object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner.
The Court or Tribunal shall have to assess the damages objectively and exclude from consideration any speculation or fancy, though some conjecture with reference to the nature of disability and its consequences, is inevitable.
A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury.
This means that he is to be compensated for his inability to lead a full life, his inability to enjoy those normal amenities which he would have enjoyed but for the injuries, and his inability to earn as much as he used to earn or could have earned.
Total permanent disability refers to a person's inability to perform any avocation or employment related activities as a result of the accident.
By considering the dictums of Hon'ble Supreme Court and Our Hon'ble High Court and also evidence led by the medical officer, It is appears to Court that, the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries.
The petition discloses that the petitioner was doing Driving work.
It means, the petitioner is not in position to do the earlier work effectively.
